# R5.41 — Deterministic central protocol materialization

Implements `docs/tickets/211_R5.41__protocol.md` (seq 211 of 246) —
the M-H slice: `materialize_protocol(&ProtocolDecl) ->
Result<MaterializedProtocol, ProtocolError>`, a pure records-in
materializer that validates the **supplied** eligible
manifest/split/quotas/seed (every value an external gated input,
never chosen here) and yields the frozen finite-manifest protocol
record — outcome-blind 30-task no-replacement selection under equal
within-stratum weights, task-level fair lane coin assigning the two
frozen arms to identical lanes interleaved over five rounds,
first-slot bindings, and the phase/analysis-family/stop identities,
sealed under a derived `protocol_id` commitment (REQ-D-007).
Engineered machinery only — no participant data, no live execution,
no task/seed/quota choice, no scientific claim.

Requirement ids stamped: **REQ-D-007, REQ-D-101, REQ-D-102,
REQ-D-103, REQ-E-011, REQ-B-101, REQ-B-103, REQ-B-106** (primary);
contributing only: none — no second primary owner.

## What changed

- `crates/hh-eval/src/central_protocol.rs` — the materializer:
  seeded `idp_digest` ranks (the `expand::order_key` scheme) under
  `central_protocol.{select,order,coin,slot}`; per-stratum top-rank
  selection; five-round × two-arm interleaved schedule (300 slots);
  `protocol_id = idp_digest("central_protocol", canonical(record
  minus id))` minted **last** inside one `Result` — every refusal
  gate runs before selection and no prefix is an admitted state.
  Closed `ProtocolError` (30 variants): outcome-selected/unpublished
  exclusions, `DevOverlap`/`ConflictingTask`/`ExclusionEligible`/
  `LateSplit`, `UndeclaredStratum`/`DuplicateStratum`/
  `QuotaMismatch`/`InsufficientHeldOut` (never a silent smaller
  manifest), `ArmSet`, `PolicySearch`/`TaskConditioned`/
  `ArtificialPressure`, `ConcurrencyCap`/`ArmConcurrency`/
  `OrderPolicy`, `RetryCeiling`/`UnfrozenRetryClasses`/
  `WrongAnswerRetry`, `UnknownWarmth`/`Drift`/`SupportMismatch`/
  `RolesChanged`, `PhaseIdentity`/`FamilyMismatch`/`StopIdentity`,
  `ChangedAfterSubjects`, `PilotRelabel`, `MissingKey`.
- `crates/hh-eval/tests/r5_41.rs` — 16-test battery: positive
  determinism/identity/schedule legs and the full typed-negative
  union, including the three close-review refusals.
- ADR-0419 (landing decisions + refusal vocabulary; dated
  2026-11-03 amendment note for the self-review repairs).
- `docs/build/runs/R5.41.md` — run ledger with the per-target
  coverage mapping (engineered D/E achieved; R/P + actual-execution
  E stay owed to later stages and R5.49 — evidence dependency,
  never dispatch).

## Deviation (conspicuous)

**1,601 changed source/test lines vs the ≤800 trigger (~2.0×)** —
1,537 (~1.9×) measured at the `ace07fea` checkpoint stop plus 64
close-review repair lines (same compound predicate; refusal set
only grew). Recorded Deviation, accepted per the scoped **AMEND**
ruling `7c788f70`
(`docs/build/planning/2026-11-03_R5.41-split-review.md`): M-H :147
is one scope sentence binding materialize+validate as one compound
predicate (no written contingency); `materialize_protocol` mints
`protocol_id` last inside one `Result` — no prefix is an admitted
state; every candidate cut is mid-predicate or non-curative (impl
leg alone ~960). Stopped correctly at the trigger; consistent with
the 25-AMEND/3-SPLIT history. Honest trip: review, not redesign.

## Design decisions

- hh-eval is the only cycle-free home consuming the M-A
  `MethodMetadata`/slot vocabulary *and* the owning §6.3
  `SchedulingPolicy`/`ReattemptPolicy` records unchanged (hh-lab
  cannot consume hh-eval) — ADR-0419 D1.
- `protocol_id` is a derived `idp_digest` commitment under the
  existing domain idiom — no new `RecordKind`, event class, wire
  name or dependency (I-01/I-02).
- Validation order is refusal-first: change-control/relabel/
  drift/warmth/support → zero-search/policy shape → arms →
  lanes/scheduling → retries → exclusions/split → pools/quotas →
  identities → selection/coin/schedule → identity mint. The only
  `Ok` is post-validation.
